text: When you design a REST API, you should follow some simple best practices. First, use clear and meaningful endpoints, such as /users or /orders, so developers can easily understand what each resource does. Second, always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success, 404 when something is not found, and 500 for server errors. Third, write good documentation that explains every endpoint, its parameters, and its responses. Finally, use versioning, for example /v1/users, so that future changes do not break existing applications. Following these practices makes your API easier to use, maintain, and trust.
